To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the metal species present in xylem sap of plants grown in metal-rich environments are mostly inorganic and are mainly in the form of simple complexes with organic acids and that the metal species in phloem sap of plants grown under normal conditions are mainly metal complexes with amino acid ligands, and the metal-ligand stoichiometries of the complexes are not always 1:1.

the metal-ligand complex in xylem and/or phloem sapes is still unknown.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the identification of the metal-ligand complex in plant fluids is still an ongoing challenge and that the use of analytical tools based on mass spectometry is a promising strategy to identify the metal-ligands species involved in the long distance metal translocation in plants.
the identification of the metal species involved in the long distance transport of metals in plants is still a challenge.
the use of new analytical techniques and approaches has allowed us to identify metal complexes present in plant fluids, which have been proposed to be involved in metal translocation in plants.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the metal species in plant fluids are not as simple as previously thought.
the identification of metal-ligand and metal-protein species in plant fluids is a very challenging task that requires a multidisciplinary approach.
there is a need to develop analytical tools that can be applied to plant fluids in order to identify metal species and metal-ligands complexes in situ.
